Salesforce runs the world's largest CRM platform and is rebuilding itself around Agentforce, Data 360, Slack, MuleSoft, Tableau and Informatica. Shares have been dragged down by the "SaaSpocalypse" story. Jim Cramer summed up the fear on Mad Money: "people feared that something like Claude would obviate Salesforce entirely." Agentforce Growth at 14x Forward Earnings Looks Mispriced

A forward P/E of 14 and a free cash flow yield of 8.19% appeal to bulls, especially for a company whose Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached about $3.9 billion, up 210%. Agentforce alone exceeded $1.5 billion, up 240%. Current RPO growth accelerated to 14% from 13%, and net new AOV growth was the strongest in four years.

Salesforce (CRM) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this customer-management software developer have returned -6.8%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Salesforce falls in, has lost 13.4%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Salesforce is expected to post earnings of $3.43 per share, indicating a change of +5.5% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $16.72 points to a change of +33.6% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $16.03 indicates a change of -4.1% from what Salesforce is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Salesforce is rated Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Yahoo Finance reported on November 5 that the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 3.4%, or more than 1,800 points, while the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5% into correction territory. Chip stocks took the brunt of the damage, with AI chip designers and memory makers among the hardest hit. The slide erased the gains from a day earlier, when the Dow had jumped 3% for its best session of 2026 after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, Yahoo Finance wrote on November 4. By mid-session Thursday, the index was heading for its worst second day after a midterm election in data going back to 1896, the outlet noted.

The Dow's Safe-Haven Run Cracks

For most of the week, the Dow had looked like the sheltered corner of the market. Yahoo Finance reported on November 2 that the Dow edged up 0.4% while the Nasdaq dropped roughly 1% as investors rotated out of technology names and into consumer cyclical and financial services shares, which left the Dow looking like the market's relative winner. On Thursday, that cushion gave way, as the focus turned to what a Democratic Congress could mean for the AI buildout, and for the data centers driving it in particular. You might also be interested in reading our piece on how the AI chip leader's growth compares with the cloud software giant's.

The reversal was fast and violent. Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at an equity research firm, pointed out that the VIX volatility index posted its biggest one-day jump in more than two years. It took the Nasdaq just six minutes on Thursday to erase its entire post-election rally, and even Wednesday's winners such as the iPhone maker turned lower. That Wednesday buying had been helped by falling oil prices, while the Windows maker jumped 6% to a record high.

A Jobs Report Steadies the Tape

Friday brought a partial rebound. Yahoo Finance reported on November 6 that the US added 165,000 jobs in October, and the Nasdaq gained 1.9% while the S&P 500 rose 1% and the Dow added 0.1%. Atlassian (TEAM) stock fell 16.2% on Friday, November 6, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 0.3%. After the close on Thursday, November 5, the company reported first-quarter results for fiscal 2027 that beat analysts' estimates for both earnings and revenue. So why did a quarter that beat estimates send the shares this far down?

Atlassian Beat Estimates But Expects Slower Cloud Growth

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Atlassian earned an adjusted $1.65 per share, compared to the $1.39 analysts expected. Revenue reached $1.8 billion, above the $1.71 billion estimate, and management said on the November 5 call that cloud revenue grew 31%.

The shares fell on what Atlassian said about cloud growth. While the company raised its outlook for the full year, its guidance pointed to slower cloud growth, and the stock sold off as soon as the numbers came out. On the call, an analyst said the second-quarter cloud revenue guide implied about 4 points of slowdown, more than the guidance from 90 days earlier had implied. Some analysts called the worry over slower cloud growth an overreaction.

Management stressed other figures on the call. RPO, representing revenue customers have signed up for but Atlassian has not yet booked, grew 44% to $4.7 billion. More than 3,000 customers have now upgraded to the Teamwork Collection, seven times as many as a year earlier.

Did Other Software Stocks Fall With Atlassian?

Atlassian's software peers also fell, though by far less, even as the wider technology sector rose. The technology sector fund XLK gained 1.5% in the same session. Among the companies on the Trefis list of Atlassian's peers, Asana fell 5.0% and Salesforce fell 3.9%.

Asana saw the largest of those peer falls, yet its decline was less than a third of Atlassian's drop. Atlassian's stock moved on its own report, not with its group.

One report can knock a single stock down 16.2%. Here's how to build a portfolio for a crash and a rally.

Where Does Atlassian Stock Stand Now?

Over the prior 365 days, Atlassian had not fallen this much in a single session. Its last move this large went the other way: a 35.3% gain on August 7, 2026.

The drop leaves the shares down 4.8% over the past 12 months, against a 9.8% gain for the S&P 500. Friday's close of $153.68 sits well below the stock's highest close of the year, $227.61 on October 23, 2026, but remains far above the year's lowest close, $57.15 on April 10, 2026. The stock returned 67.8% over the past six months, yet it fell 24.5% over the past month alone.

Investors interested in stocks from the Internet - Software sector have probably already heard of Salesforce (CRM) and Autodesk (ADSK). But which of these two stocks presents investors with the better value opportunity right now? Let's take a closer look.

Everyone has their own methods for finding great value opportunities, but our model includes pairing an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system with a strong Zacks Rank. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

Salesforce has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), while Autodesk has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) right now. This system places an emphasis on companies that have seen positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that CRM is likely seeing its earnings outlook improve to a greater extent. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use.

CRM currently has a forward P/E ratio of 13.31, while ADSK has a forward P/E of 21.32. We also note that CRM has a PEG ratio of 0.78. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. ADSK currently has a PEG ratio of 1.37.

Another notable valuation metric for CRM is its P/B ratio of 4.77. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, ADSK has a P/B of 16.63.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to CRM's Value grade of B and ADSK's Value grade of C.

CRM sticks out from ADSK in both our Zacks Rank and Style Scores models, so value investors will likely feel that CRM is the better option right now.
